headline: Two bomb-like objects recovered from Demra house, one detained
summary: Police recovered two bomb-like objects during a raid in Dhaka's Demra area while searching for suspects in a separate attack on police.
details: Police recovered two bomb-like objects from a house in West Boxnagar, Demra, on Sunday night. The operation took place at the intersection of Sakine Garib-er Newaj Mosque Road.
The recovery happened during a raid to arrest suspects involved in a recent attack on police at Jatrabari's Jonopod intersection.
According to a CTTC Bomb Disposal Unit official, one of the objects has been neutralized, while work to neutralize the second one is ongoing.
One suspect has been detained in connection with the case and is being questioned by the police.
caption:
Two bomb-like objects found in a residential house in Demra!

Police recovered two bomb-like objects from a house in West Boxnagar, Demra, on Sunday night. The operation took place at the intersection of Sakine Garib-er Newaj Mosque Road.

The recovery happened during a raid to arrest suspects involved in a recent attack on police at Jatrabari's Jonopod intersection.

According to a CTTC Bomb Disposal Unit official, one of the objects has been neutralized, while work to neutralize the second one is ongoing.

One suspect has been detained in connection with the case and is being questioned by the police.

headline_marked: DU student [[detained and intimidated by hall provost]] over Facebook post
headline: DU student detained and intimidated by hall provost over Facebook post
summary: Students of Fazlul Huq Muslim Hall are protesting and demanding the resignation of Provost Prof. Elias Al Mamun following allegations of student harassment.
details: A student of Dhaka University's Fazlul Huq Muslim Hall, Md. Ibrahim, has accused Provost Prof. Elias Al Mamun of detaining him in his office for about 90 minutes and intimidating him over a Facebook post.
Ibrahim, a student of the Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering department, claims his phone was forcibly taken by staff and the door was locked to prevent him from leaving.
The student alleges he was threatened with the cancellation of his hall seat, expulsion from the university, and a lawsuit under the Cyber Security Act, and was forced to sign a written statement.
Provost Prof. Elias Al Mamun has denied the allegations, stating that the student had written 'incorrect' things about him on Facebook and was called in for a discussion.
The Provost claims the student was recording the conversation, which led to the request for the phone, and that the student himself deleted the recording.
Following the incident, residential students began protesting in front of the hall office after 9 PM, demanding the Provost's resignation.
A delegation of student leaders from the hall parliament and DUCSU met with the Provost, but they report that he refused to provide CCTV footage of the incident.
Protesting students have declared the Provost 'unwanted' and vowed to keep him besieged until he resigns from his position.
caption:
Locked in a room for 90 minutes and threatened with expulsion—a DU student claims he was tortured by his own hall provost over a Facebook post.

A student of Dhaka University's Fazlul Huq Muslim Hall, Md. Ibrahim, has accused Provost Prof. Elias Al Mamun of detaining him in his office for about 90 minutes and intimidating him over a Facebook post.

Ibrahim, a student of the Robotics and Mechatronics Engineering department, claims his phone was forcibly taken by staff and the door was locked to prevent him from leaving.

The student alleges he was threatened with the cancellation of his hall seat, expulsion from the university, and a lawsuit under the Cyber Security Act, and was forced to sign a written statement.

Provost Prof. Elias Al Mamun has denied the allegations, stating that the student had written 'incorrect' things about him on Facebook and was called in for a discussion.

The Provost claims the student was recording the conversation, which led to the request for the phone, and that the student himself deleted the recording.

Following the incident, residential students began protesting in front of the hall office after 9 PM, demanding the Provost's resignation.

A delegation of student leaders from the hall parliament and DUCSU met with the Provost, but they report that he refused to provide CCTV footage of the incident.

Protesting students have declared the Provost 'unwanted' and vowed to keep him besieged until he resigns from his position.

#DhakaUniversity #DU #StudentProtest #CampusNews #Bangladesh

Source: Prothom Alo, Somoy News
